title: Run record
description: One line of the JSONL run log - the ONLY interface between the Rust harness and the Python analysis (see docs/DESIGN.md). It is also the archival artifact: a reviewer must be able to recompute every published number from these lines alone, years later. That is why provenance is required rather than convenient.

model.description: quantisation is REQUIRED and load-bearing. Calibration metrics are not comparable across quant levels (M-ratio profiles decorrelate entirely), so a record without it cannot be placed on a leaderboard at all.

sampling.description: Confidence is sensitive to these. Recording them is what makes a run reproducible. REQUIRED as of 0.3.0: they were optional before, so the docs' claim that provenance was 'enforced in the schema' was false — a record with no sampling block validated and scored.

think.description: false is REQUIRED for reasoning models such as qwen3.5, which otherwise emit into the thinking field leaving response empty.

elicitation.description: Which confidence-elicitation strategy produced the numbers. Pluggable by design: verbalised confidence may not survive the validity screen.

samples.description: For self-consistency: how many samples were drawn.

signals.description: The metacognitive readouts. fok is prospective (pre-solve), jol retrospective (post-solve) - Nelson-Narens, per arXiv 2605.14186.

agreement.description: Self-consistency: fraction of samples agreeing with the modal answer.

answered.description: Did the model answer rather than abstain? Distinct from correctness - an abstention on an unanswerable item is a SUCCESS.

correct.description: null when not applicable (e.g. correctly abstained on an unanswerable item).

schema_valid.description: Did the response parse against the expected schema? A false here is a harness/model-format problem, NOT evidence about metacognition - keep it separate so the two are never conflated.

choice.description: Selected option letter, as PRESENTED (i.e. after any permutation), not as stored canonically.

premise_challenged.description: Model flagged the question as resting on something false. Without this, a correct rebuttal is indistinguishable from credulity.

ollama_total_ns.description: Ollama's own total_duration in ns. Excludes our queue wait; the gap against total_ms is the queueing cost.

harness_version.description: Prompt-set and code version. A prompt edit invalidates prior results, so this must change with it.

item.description: Item metadata copied in at write time. Deliberately duplicated from the item file so the run log alone supports stratification by category and domain - a reviewer recomputing a published number years later should not need the exact item file too.

forced_choice.description: Item presented with options. Forced choice gives a well-defined Type-1 decision (required for meta-d') and a reachable negative class (required for Type-2 AUROC).

recovered_from_thinking.description: The reply was parsed out of `thinking` because `response` was empty. Its OWN field, not `error`: error is the hard-failure channel the CLI points readers at, and putting a benign warning there made `error != null` ambiguous.

permutation.description: Option ordering applied, as indices into the canonical order. Required to rescore a choice: a letter resolved against canonical order scores every permuted item wrong.
